userStories.title: Add the wf-repair role and workflowRepairOp
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Give repairs their own canonical session role, operation and leftover-commit identity while preserving default branch fixes.

**Motivation** — Its tokens are booked with the branch fix, and after the last round the ledger says only `CI failed`, with no record of which check or step is still red.

**Approach** — 1. **Role and op.** `wf-repair` joins `CanonicalSessionRole`. `workflowRepairOp` (`src/operations/workflow-repair.ts`) is `workflowBranchFixOp` with `name: "workflow-repair"` and `session: { role: "wf-repair", lifetime: "fresh" }`. Its tools, model resolution, timeout, writable report, soft-interrupt hop body, parser and recover are the same. Because the token meter keys `byRole` by the dispatch's `sessionRole`, the new role books separately with no meter change. `runBranchFix` takes `kind?: "fix" | "repair"`. `"repair"` dispatches `workflowRepairOp` and commits leftover edits as `wf-repair`, so the commit reads `chore(_run): auto-commit after wf-repair session`. Rule delivery treats `wf-repair` exactly like `wf-branch-fix`.

**Scope** — In: CanonicalSessionRole and KNOWN_SESSION_ROLES, both rule-delivery role lists, the new op and operations barrel export, and kind-based dispatch/auto-commit in runBranchFix. Out: workflow/bot caller routing and the verification rule (US-002), CI metadata (US-003), CI prompt selection (US-004), evidence (US-005/006), and review setup (US-007). The `costUsd: 0` booked for native-agent repair tokens in nax#2642 is a cost-estimation issue in the dispatch events, not a role issue; this feature only separates the role. The session-role table in `.nax/rules/adapter-wiring.md` gains `wf-repair` as a manual follow-up after the run (`.nax/` is read-only to the run).

**Interface** — Verbatim target declarations:
```typescript
// src/operations/workflow-repair.ts (exported from @/operations)
export const workflowRepairOp: RunOperationWithHooks<WorkflowBranchFixInput, ImplementerReply, WorkflowOpConfig, "hopBody" | "recover">;
```
`BranchFixInput` gains `kind?: "fix" | "repair"`; omitted kind preserves the existing operation, prompt and commit role.

**Implementation and test notes** — Mirror the existing typed op, preserve soft-interrupt and recovery behavior, and keep every current non-abort leftover-commit path. Extend the makeScriptedCallOp/commit-argument harness in test/unit/workflow/branch-fix.test.ts; old tests without kind keep wf-branch-fix. Add test/unit/operations/workflow-repair.test.ts to assert the public op and its inherited behaviors. Existing role membership tests need no expectation rewrite.

userStories.title: Route workflow and bot repairs to wf-repair
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Route workflow CI/final-gate and bot repair/prepare sessions to wf-repair and require explicit concerns for checks unavailable locally.

**Motivation** — `nax bot fix`'s repair step (`repairStep`, modes `repair` and `prepare`) has the same identity problem: it calls `runBranchFix`, so it books under `wf-branch-fix` too.

**Approach** — 2. **Routing.** `FeatureSteps.branchFix` takes `opts.repair?: true`. `buildFeatureEnv` maps it to `kind: "repair"`. `gateRepairStep` and `ciRepairStep` pass `repair: true`; `branchFixStep` is unchanged. Each call stays one line (`ciRepairStep` spreads `prUrl` into the options object instead of its current two-call ternary), because `feature-steps.ts` has 3 lines left before US-004 moves the CI repair out. Bot `repairStep` passes `kind: "repair"` in both modes; bot `fixStep` is unchanged. `REPAIR_VERIFICATION_RULE` is added to `src/prompts/builders/workflow-implementer-builder.ts` beside `WORKFLOW_REPLY_CONTRACT`, exported from `@/prompts`, and bot `buildBotPrFixPrompt`'s `repair` and `prepare` modes include it.

**Scope** — In: repair option forwarding through FeatureSteps/buildFeatureEnv, one-line gate/CI calls, bot repair/prepare kind, and the shared rule in bot repair/prepare instructions. Out: new op internals (US-001), Actions steps (US-003), ciRound/CI prompt and module extraction (US-004), CI reply evidence (US-005/006), review builds (US-007). Workflow final-gate repair changes its session role to `wf-repair` but keeps the branch-fix prompt. Bot `fix` mode's prompt and role are unchanged. Recording the `concerns` of the bot repair and the workflow final-gate repair replies; only the workflow CI repair records its concerns.

**Interface** — Target additions from the spec:
```typescript
export const REPAIR_VERIFICATION_RULE: string;
```
`FeatureSteps.branchFix` takes `(findings, opts?: { readonly prUrl?: string; readonly repair?: true })` at this stage; ciRound is introduced by US-004. Bot repair inputs carry `kind: "repair"`. The exact rule is: If you cannot run a check here (for example the sandbox blocks its network, or its tool is missing), reply DONE_WITH_CONCERNS and name each such check in "concerns". Never reply DONE for a check you only reasoned about. The `repair` and `prepare` modes end with `- ${REPAIR_VERIFICATION_RULE}`; `fix` is unchanged.

**Implementation and test notes** — The feature-env.test.ts makeScriptedCallOp harness drives the real buildFeatureEnv dispatch/provider seams; do not replace this with testing only a copied option mapper. Add feature-steps-repair-routing.test.ts. In feature-steps-ci-repair.test.ts, US-012 AC-1 changes from { prUrl } to { prUrl, repair: true }, and ci-without-url/gate-with-url gain { repair: true }; ordinary branch fix still has one argument and only CI forwards the PR URL. In integration/bot/repair-step.test.ts, the exact AC-8/9/10 input gains kind: repair while prompt and patch assertions stay intact. Regenerate final-gates-repair.json through feature-machine equivalence with NAX_UPDATE_WORKFLOW_GOLDEN=1 and verify the only golden change is the second argument on gate-repair calls.

routing.reasoning: Routes session roles through workflow and bot entry points while preserving provider and prepare boundaries; sessions and role routing trigger the security override.

modifiedFiles.reason: "US-012 AC-1 forwards the published PR URL and retains C1" expects the `branchFix` calls to equal `[[[C1], { prUrl }]]`; the CI repair now also passes `repair: true`, so it expects `[[[C1], { prUrl, repair: true }]]`. The `"%s stays unbound"` cases expect a one-argument call for `ci-without-url` and `gate-with-url`; both repairs now pass `{ repair: true }`, so each expects `[[[finding], { repair: true }]]`. The invariant that only the CI repair forwards the PR URL is unchanged, and "US-012 AC-2 ordinary branch fix uses one argument" is unchanged.

"AC-8/9/10 builds repair prompt with every tail and increments round" expects `runBranchFix` to have been called with exactly `{ findings, model, toolProviders, prompt }`; the repair now also passes `kind: "repair"`, so the expected object gains `kind: "repair"`. Its prompt and patch assertions are unchanged.

the golden trace records each `branchFix` call's arguments, and its final-gate repair calls hold one argument (`[[{ "id": "G1", ... }]]`); `gateRepairStep` now passes `{ repair: true }`, so those calls gain that second argument. Regenerate the golden by running the feature-machine equivalence test with `NAX_UPDATE_WORKFLOW_GOLDEN=1` and check that the only diff is that second argument on the gate-repair calls. The invariant that the machine's step sequence matches the golden is unchanged.

userStories.title: Read failed and subsequently skipped Actions steps
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Enrich failed GitHub Actions checks with the first failed step and the skipped steps after it without changing log excerpts or other forge paths.

**Motivation** — A job stops at its first failing step.

**Approach** — 3. **Job steps.** `FailedCheck` gains `failedStep?: string` and `skippedSteps?: readonly string[]`. For a GitHub Actions check, after the job log is read, `readJobSteps` (`src/forge/job-steps.ts`) runs `gh api --hostname <host> repos/<repo>/actions/jobs/<id>`. The first step whose `conclusion` is `"failure"` is `failedStep`; the names of the steps after it whose `conclusion` is `"skipped"` are `skippedSteps`, in job order. Reading the steps is best effort: a failed command, an unparsable reply, a reply without a `steps` array, or a job with no failed step leaves both fields absent and changes nothing else. GitLab jobs and non-Actions check runs get neither field and make no extra call.

**Scope** — In: internal job-steps reader, additive FailedCheck fields, and toFailedCheck integration after the existing log read, including when that read reports logUnavailable. Out: finding/prompt consumption (US-004), evidence persistence (US-005/006), roles/routing (US-001/002), review build (US-007). nax#2642 gap 1 (log unavailable while the Actions run is in progress) was fixed by nax#2659; this feature does not change how the job log is read. GitLab jobs expose no step list, so a GitLab failed check never carries `failedStep` or `skippedSteps`. Reading CI workflow files to list a job's steps; the steps come only from the Actions jobs API. A job whose step ended `cancelled` or `timed_out` gets no `failedStep`; only a step with conclusion `failure` is named.

**Interface** — Verbatim new declarations:
```typescript
// src/forge/job-steps.ts (internal to src/forge)
export interface JobSteps { readonly failedStep?: string; readonly skippedSteps?: readonly string[] }
export async function readJobSteps(ref: PrRef, jobId: string, deps: ForgeDeps, cwd: string): Promise<JobSteps>;
```
`FailedCheck` target: `{ name; url?; excerpt; logUnavailable?; failedStep?: string; skippedSteps?: readonly string[] }`. Preserve readonly fields and the existing logUnavailable contract.

**Failure handling** — Non-zero command, invalid JSON, missing steps array and no step with conclusion failure each leave both optional fields absent. Excerpts remain unchanged. An empty suffix of skipped steps leaves no skippedSteps key.

**Implementation and test notes** — Inject all API commands through ForgeDeps. Extend the readFailedChecks seam as well as unit-testing readJobSteps. The existing githubFixture returns its check-runs JSON for the new endpoint, which has no steps array, so no existing fixtures need rewriting. With one Actions check the jobs request is third, after listing and log; calls[1] must remain the log. Keep GitLab and CircleCI call counts unchanged. Avoid importing ci-failures from job-steps if doing so creates a cycle.

userStories.title: Persist CI repair concerns and targeted checks
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Persist workflow CI repair targets and accumulated reply concerns in result.json, ledger notes and the end-of-run concerns summary.

**Motivation** — The workflow never reads the branch-fix reply's `concerns`, so nothing recorded that half the job went unchecked.

**Approach** — Relevant portions of Design 6, **Evidence**, verbatim:
- `ciRepairTargets` is written by `publishStep` whenever it decides a repair: each failed check's `name`, plus `failedStep` when known.
- `ciRepairConcerns` is appended by `ciRepairStep` as `r<N>: <concerns>` when the repair's reply carries non-empty `concerns`. The same text goes to the ledger as `CI repair r<N> concerns: <concerns>`.
- How `publishStep` gets the checks: `ciRepairDecision` keeps its signature and still returns the findings array (its tests call it directly). A new `ciRepairPlan(env, rec, out, head)` in `ci-repair-steps.ts` returns `{ findings, targets } | undefined` from the same single read, and `ciRepairDecision` returns `(await ciRepairPlan(...))?.findings`. `publishStep` calls `ciRepairPlan`.

`WorkflowSummaryView` gains `ciRemaining` (each `<name>` or `<name> at step "<step>"`) and `ciRepairConcerns`.
`summaryLine` appends `CI still failing: <a>, <b>` and `CI repair concerns: <a>; <b>`.

This story implements the targets/concerns portion; the ciRemaining field and its summary clause in those shared design sentences belong to US-006.

**Scope** — In: CiCheckRef, optional ciRepairTargets/ciRepairConcerns, ciRepairPlan and compatibility wrapper, target patches from publish, concern patches/ledger notes from CI repair, graph produces updates, conditional summary-view concerns and end-of-run text. Out: terminal-CI reading/classification/ciRemaining and its summary text (US-006), builders/extraction (US-004), and bot-review setup (US-007). Recording the `concerns` of the bot repair and the workflow final-gate repair replies; only the workflow CI repair records its concerns. Classifying a failure as new when a second repair round is decided; only the final remaining-CI read classifies. The PR's draft reason for a failed CI stays `CI failed`; the remaining checks and concerns go to the ledger, `result.json` and the end-of-run summary only.

**Interface** — Verbatim target types/fields for this story:
```typescript
CiCheckRef = { readonly name: string; readonly failedStep?: string };
ciRepairTargets?: readonly CiCheckRef[];
ciRepairConcerns?: readonly string[];
```
The summary-view target addition is `ciRepairConcerns?: readonly string[] | undefined`. `ci-repair` produces `["ciRepairRounds", "ciRepairFindings", "ciRepairConcerns"]`; `publish` also produces `ciRepairTargets`. Keep ciRepairDecision's existing signature and findings-only result.

**Failure handling** — Repair reply has no `concerns` (empty or absent), or the session failed with no reply: No ledger concerns line; `ciRepairConcerns` not patched. Add no empty optional keys. Concerns append to existing round-labelled history, rather than replacing it. Preserve repair-decision log readability and cost/round checks.

**Implementation and test notes** — Extend the ci-repair-steps.ts created by US-004. Drive concern evidence at ciRepairStep and target selection at publishStep using the existing machine/publish harnesses. Build findings and targets from one CI read; do not call the compatibility wrapper and then read again for targets. The existing sink persists complete records to result.json, so no duplicate evidence writer or schema migration is needed. Update expectedProduces in feature-graph.test.ts for ciRepairConcerns and ciRepairTargets. Extend run-summary.test.ts and workflow-end-report.test.ts for conditional forwarding and exact summary text. Add ci-repair-steps-evidence.test.ts.

userStories.title: Record and summarize CI still failing after the last repair
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Read final red CI after spent repair rounds, classify checks against the last targets and surface the remaining checks without scheduling another agent.

**Motivation** — Its tokens are booked with the branch fix, and after the last round the ledger says only `CI failed`, with no record of which check or step is still red.

**Approach** — Relevant portions of Design 6, **Evidence**, verbatim:
- `ciRemaining` is written by `publishStep` when all of these hold: `readCiFailures` exists, the outcome is `draft`, CI is `failed`, the publish has a URL and a HEAD, at least one repair round ran, and the rounds are spent (`ciRepairRounds >= workflow.ciRepairRounds`). In that case the failed checks are read, whatever the cost state, since the read runs no agent. This condition and `ciRepairDecision`'s (rounds left) never both hold, so a publish reads the failed checks at most once.
- How `publishStep` gets the checks: `ciRepairDecision` keeps its signature and still returns the findings array (its tests call it directly). A new `ciRepairPlan(env, rec, out, head)` in `ci-repair-steps.ts` returns `{ findings, targets } | undefined` from the same single read, and `ciRepairDecision` returns `(await ciRepairPlan(...))?.findings`. `publishStep` calls `ciRepairPlan`. The remaining-CI read is a separate function, `ciRemainingAfterRepair(env, rec, out, head)`, which calls `env.steps.readCiFailures` directly, not `readCiFailuresForRepair`, so it never writes the `(repairing)` note. On a throw it writes only `CI logs unavailable: <message>`; on an empty list it writes no note. Each check is recorded with `newFailure: true` unless a target has the same `name` and the same `failedStep`. The ledger gets `CI still failing after <N> repair round(s): <check>[ at step "<step>"] (new failure|still failing)`, with checks joined by `; `.

`WorkflowSummaryView` gains `ciRemaining` (each `<name>` or `<name> at step "<step>"`) and `ciRepairConcerns`.
`summaryLine` appends `CI still failing: <a>, <b>` and `CI repair concerns: <a>; <b>`.

The PR's draft reason stays `CI failed`: `publish` posts it before the CI read (ruled out of scope).

**Scope** — In: CiRemainingCheck/optional ciRemaining, terminal read helper and publish wiring, comparison to US-005 targets, exact terminal ledger notes, graph produces, conditional summary-view remaining checks and end-of-run formatting. Out: introducing concerns/targets/ciRepairPlan (already US-005), changes to repair prompts or routing (US-001/002/004), and review build setup (US-007). Classifying a failure as new when a second repair round is decided; only the final remaining-CI read classifies. The default of `workflow.ciRepairRounds` stays 1. The PR's draft reason for a failed CI stays `CI failed`; the remaining checks and concerns go to the ledger, `result.json` and the end-of-run summary only.

**Interface** — Verbatim target types/fields:
```typescript
CiRemainingCheck = CiCheckRef & { readonly newFailure: boolean };
ciRemaining?: readonly CiRemainingCheck[];
```
`WorkflowSummaryView` gains `ciRemaining?: readonly string[] | undefined`. `publish` also produces `ciRemaining`. Extend `ci-repair-steps.ts` with `ciRemainingAfterRepair(env, rec, out, head)`; reuse the upstream ciRepairPlan and preserve ciRepairDecision's signature.

**Failure handling** — Remaining-CI read throws: Ledger `CI logs unavailable: <message>`; no `ciRemaining`. Remaining-CI read returns no check: No `ciRemaining`, no still-failing note. The terminal helper also must not emit a `(repairing)` note, including empty responses.

**Implementation and test notes** — Drive ACs through publishStep carrying ciRepairTargets, including a cost-limited run, mismatched/same steps, no repair ever run, green CI, ready outcome, thrown reads and empty reads. This is a non-agent read and must bypass cost gating. Existing graph persistence carries the new optional field into result.json. Update expectedProduces.publish in feature-graph.test.ts. In feature-steps-ci-repair-decision.test.ts rename AC-13 'spent repair rounds read no CI logs' to say spent rounds decide no repair; assert one terminal read and no ci-repair exit, preserving the round-to-spare one-read control. Direct ciRepairDecision still returns no repair with spent rounds. Add ci-repair-steps-remaining.test.ts and extend summary/end-report tests.

userStories.title: Build bot review worktrees and distinguish checks that could not start
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Build trusted fresh bot-review worktrees after installation and report setup-blocked checks as could not start rather than defects in the change.

**Motivation** — `nax bot review` runs `execution.preRun` (the install) in a fresh worktree, but nothing builds that library.

**Approach** — 7. **Bot review build.** `reviewBuildSteps(checks)` (`src/bot/checks.ts`) turns the `command` of the gate named exactly `build` into steps: a list becomes one step per element, and every step gets `timeoutSeconds: REVIEW_BUILD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`. A `build` gate never carries a `setup` (`resolveGateCommands` gives only `e2e` one), so `setup` is ignored. `REVIEW_BUILD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` is `DEFAULT_GATE_TIMEOUT_MS / 1000` (900), derived from the gate runner's own default, as `DERIVED_INSTALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` is for the install; the build is the same gate command, so it gets the same bound. `DEFAULT_GATE_TIMEOUT_MS` is added to the `@/finish` barrel's `./gates/quality` exports.
- `prepareReviewChecks` runs these steps through `runPreRunSteps` after a successful install, but only when the list is non-empty and the checkout is not `inPlace`.
- A `PRE_RUN_FAILED` from the build records `buildFailed: <command>`; any other error propagates.
- `ReviewPreparation` gains `buildRan: readonly string[]`: every command of `reviewBuildSteps(checks)` once the build was attempted (including the commands after a failing one), and `[]` on every other return path (static mode, install failed, in-place, no `build` gate). The checkout state's `setup` lists the install commands followed by `buildRan`, and its `setupFailed` is the install's failure or else the build's.
- `postPrReview` forwards `buildFailed` into the summary input beside `preRunFailed` (`src/bot/post.ts`), and the review summary gains the line `Build step failed (<command>); checks that import built workspace packages may not have started.`
- The commands come only from the trusted base snapshot (`resolveBotChecks`), and static mode (an untrusted PR) still runs nothing.

8. **"Could not start".** `buildBotPrReviewPrompt` appends `COULD_NOT_START_RULE` as the last line of its `## Checkout state` section. That section exists only when `checkoutState` is set, which `reviewEnvironment` does only outside static mode; no new heading is added, so the pinned `## Checklist` slice, the heading order and the `## Your task` tail are unchanged. The rule: a check that stops before it runs any test did not run. It goes in `cannotVerify` as `could not start: <check>: <reason>`, naming the setup step it needs, and is never reported as a defect in the change.

**Scope** — In: reviewBuildSteps and derived timeout, finish barrel constant, trusted fresh-checkout post-install build, buildRan/buildFailed preparation fields, checkout-state setup concatenation and failure precedence, buildFailed summary forwarding/rendering, and the conditional checkout-state prompt rule. Out: repair role/routing/prompt/evidence work (US-001 through US-006). Bot review never runs per-package build overlays (`build@<package>`), only the root gate named `build`. Bot review runs no build step for an `--in-place` review, which reuses the user's existing build. Bot fix gets no build step; its bar already runs the build gate after the session. A new verdict field for checks that could not start; the reviewer reports them through `cannotVerify` with the `could not start:` prefix.

**Interface** — Verbatim new declarations:
```typescript
// src/bot/checks.ts
export const REVIEW_BUILD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: number; // DEFAULT_GATE_TIMEOUT_MS / 1000
export function reviewBuildSteps(checks: BotChecks): PreRunStepConfig[];
```
`ReviewPreparation` target: `{ checks; preRunFailed?; ci; buildFailed?: string; buildRan: readonly string[] }`. `PostReviewInput` in src/bot/post.ts and `ReviewSummaryInput` in src/bot/render-comments.ts each gain `buildFailed?: string`. `DEFAULT_GATE_TIMEOUT_MS` is exported from `@/finish`.

**Exact prompt rule** — If a check stops before it runs any test, for example because a module or workspace package cannot be resolved, it did not run: list it in "cannotVerify" as "could not start: <check>: <reason>" and name the setup step it needs. Never report it as a defect in the change.

**Failure handling** — Review install step fails: Build steps not run; `preRunFailed` recorded as today. Review build step fails (`PRE_RUN_FAILED`): `buildFailed` recorded; review still runs. Review build step throws anything else: The error propagates out of `runBotReview`. Do not catch build errors in the install catch or treat unexpected errors as setup warnings. Build commands use the existing trusted host-side runner, not a new shell path.

**Implementation and test notes** — Use review-run.test.ts's dependency harness and its #2631 real postPrReview path to verify actual summary posting, plus review-checkout-state.test.ts's captured real prompt for command order and success/failure text. Existing fixtures have no build gate, so their one-install calls and checkout-state setup text remain unchanged. Add checks-review-build.test.ts and integration/bot/review-build.test.ts; cover install-first/build-second ordering, continuation after PRE_RUN_FAILED, unrelated error propagation, in-place and static suppression, exact root-gate filtering and list order. Populate buildRan on every return path, including all commands once a multi-command build was attempted even if its runner stopped early. The prompt-only rule must not alter headings, Checklist or Your task tail.

Never report it as a defect in the change.`.

analysis:
Goal and definition of done: close #2642 and #2641 by identifying all repair sessions separately from review-driven branch fixes, giving workflow CI repair a step-aware verification brief, persisting its targets/concerns/final red checks, and building trusted fresh bot-review worktrees before review. Exactly seven stories execute entirely in packages/nax, with the binding dependency chain US-001 -> US-002; US-002 + US-003 -> US-004 -> US-005 -> US-006, and independent US-007. No changes to nax-ai, nax-agent or nax-agent-acp are needed. MCP navigation was unavailable in this host; findings below come from direct file reads and text searches, not a graph index. No runtime tests were executed while drafting this PRD.

Architecture and conventions: docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:17 identifies the injectable _deps pattern and error conventions; docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:131 identifies workflow mode as the default orchestration path; docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:149 describes the workspace boundaries. Use Bun APIs, strict TypeScript, existing barrels, and bun:test helpers. outOfScope: nax#2642 gap 1 (log unavailable while the Actions run is in progress) was fixed by nax#2659; this feature does not change how the job log is read.
The `costUsd: 0` booked for native-agent repair tokens in nax#2642 is a cost-estimation issue in the dispatch events, not a role issue; this feature only separates the role.
The PR's draft reason for a failed CI stays `CI failed`; the remaining checks and concerns go to the ledger, `result.json` and the end-of-run summary only.
Workflow final-gate repair changes its session role to `wf-repair` but keeps the branch-fix prompt.
Bot `fix` mode's prompt and role are unchanged.
Classifying a failure as new when a second repair round is decided; only the final remaining-CI read classifies.
GitLab jobs expose no step list, so a GitLab failed check never carries `failedStep` or `skippedSteps`.
Reading CI workflow files to list a job's steps; the steps come only from the Actions jobs API.
Bot review never runs per-package build overlays (`build@<package>`), only the root gate named `build`.
Bot review runs no build step for an `--in-place` review, which reuses the user's existing build.
Bot fix gets no build step; its bar already runs the build gate after the session.
A job whose step ended `cancelled` or `timed_out` gets no `failedStep`; only a step with conclusion `failure` is named.
A new verdict field for checks that could not start; the reviewer reports them through `cannotVerify` with the `could not start:` prefix.
Recording the `concerns` of the bot repair and the workflow final-gate repair replies; only the workflow CI repair records its concerns.
The session-role table in `.nax/rules/adapter-wiring.md` gains `wf-repair` as a manual follow-up after the run (`.nax/` is read-only to the run).
